description: Past probe events RealUptime recorded for one catalog service whose status feed we cannot read. For a service whose feed works, `recent_events`, `last_outage` and `reliability` are `available: false` with the reason (the vendor's declared incidents are what count, our probe events are not listed or counted), and `vendor` leads. A probe event opens only when our checks fail from two or more distant regions. Returns `last_outage` (the most recent CLOSED probe event, with its duration, regions and surfaces, or the plain statement that our checks did not fail from two or more distant regions in the N days we have checked the service) and `reliability` (per calendar month for the last 12: uptime by our checks, probe event count and minutes, from probe events only; a month before we watched the service is tracked: false with no percentage, never 100%) and `recent_events` (the probe events of the last 90 days, most recent first, at most 10, the open one included: for each, started_at, ended_at (null while open), duration, peak_level (down / partially_down), the regions and surfaces involved with their per-facet legs, and detected_by, which is always "probe"). An empty list travels with window_days and tracking_since and means our checks did not fail from two or more distant regions in that window since we started checking the service, never "this service has had no outages". Events that fail our rules are retracted and listed at https://realuptime.io/outages/corrections. The current reading travels alongside. Readings are RealUptime's own check readings, never user reports. For a service whose status feed we can read, `vendor.feed_working` is true and `vendor` holds the vendor's own declared incident from its status page: that statement leads and gives the verdict and plate, and `checks_reading` and `vendor.regional_reading` are our check reading beside it, never a second outage. Where we cannot read a feed (`vendor.feed_working` false), the answer is our checks alone. "blocked" means our check was refused, which is NOT a failed check of the service. A no-data answer is never a passing check. Our check readings are our own reading from outside, not the service's official status. `check_evidence`, when it is not null, says what a pass of this service's check shows and does not show: repeat it with any claim that the service works. Cite the returned source.url when repeating any of this.
name: list_recent_incidents
